# Regression test for native-return statement-level unwrap.
#
# When a `go:` import declares a func with shape `(T, error)`, the importer
# strips the trailing error and sets HasErrorReturn=true. The eval path that
# powers Fyne click handlers and reactive expressions must wrap such calls so
# the value can be used as a single Go expression.
#
# Before the fix, `m.rows = api.Fetch("hello")` lowered to `m.rows = api.Fetch(...)`
# (a 2-value RHS against a 1-value LHS) and refused to compile. After the fix,
# the call wraps in an IIFE that captures + discards the error.

sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --opt=main=true --out=out app.sngl
exists out/model.go

# The native call is wrapped — original raw form must not appear in an
# assignment by itself, and the wrapped IIFE must be present.
grep 'func\(\) \[\]string \{ v, _ := api\.Fetch' out/model.go

-- go.mod --
module example.com/native-err

go 1.23
-- api/api.go --
package api

func Fetch(q string) ([]string, error) { return []string{q}, nil }
-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"

output { go { fyne } }

import "go:example.com/native-err/api"

component main {
    var rows list<string> = []

    window #app(title="t") {
        vbox {
            button(text="Load", @click {
                rows = api.Fetch("hello")
            })
            text(value="rows {string(rows.length)}")
        }
    }
}
